evals.prompt: I want a video on how B-trees keep disk lookups fast. I'm a backend dev, I know binary search trees and roughly what a disk block is, but I've never looked at how a database index is laid out. Propose the narrative first, I want to iterate on it before anything gets built.
evals.expected_output: Settles the drive (the user is learning the topic: learner drive), creates the video with studio new, runs or plans fresh-context research, and returns a research/narrative.md-shaped proposal: question, answer, takeaway, a chain of chapters as claims with 'why it follows' and evidence, Cut on purpose, Vocabulary, an evidence plan, and at most three questions. Does NOT start a build.

evals.prompt: Teach me how consensus protocols like Raft work, as one of those explainer videos. I know nothing about distributed systems beyond that servers can crash. Don't ask me to judge the technical content, I can't; just make sure it's right.
evals.expected_output: Learner drive: two or three competing narratives drafted in fresh contexts, a narrative review round (studio review --narrative) on each, a chosen narrative with the reasons and the rejected ones, and a short list of risk flags. Asks only whether this is what they want to learn. No build until they say so.

evals.prompt: Explore this repo and make me a short explainer video of how its sync engine resolves conflicts. I wrote it, so I'll give you notes.
evals.expected_output: Author drive: studio new with --source pointing at the repo, explores the repo (delegating wide reads), drafts one narrative citing files, asks at most three questions, and after approval builds without reviewer rounds: narration, a stills-only look cut served on the review page, then animated cuts. Tells the user the review page URL and how to leave notes.

evals.prompt: I sent a round of notes on cut 2 of the retry-safety video: 1:42 'arrival rate is never defined', 2:10 picture: 'the table is cramped', 3:05 (no comment). Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Reads the notes with studio notes, saves them as research/annotations, maps each to its sentence, proposes changes grouped by theme before applying, changes only the chapters pointed at (script for narration notes, then studio narrate; scenes for picture notes, answered with a still first), and makes cut 3 with a changelog mapping each note to its change. Does not rebuild the whole video.
